title: Fixed-wing ambient landability
note: Facts come from the pack; ALL judgment lives here. Versioned separately from the tiles and from the app so a weight change ships as a small file, not a rebuild. Advisory only.

flags.card_text: Distribution wires are largely unmapped nationally. Absence of a wire here is not evidence there is none.

aircraft_defaults.note: AircraftProfile carries no class discriminator today, so v1 uses ONE conservative fixed-wing table and lets the REAL fields modulate it: glideRatio, vRefKts and landingOver50Ft. Class-differentiated murphy factors wait for a profile field rather than being guessed from a free-text type string. NOTE: vref_kt used to be taken from bestGlideKts, which is a different speed — best glide is flown well above approach speed. vRefKts is now its own field.

energy_model.note: Touchdown energy scales the MARGINAL surfaces only, never the hazard term, and is bounded so it can reorder marginal ground but never lift it above genuinely good ground.

distance_model.note: WHAT LANDING DISTANCE CAN AND CANNOT SAY AT PIXEL LEVEL. A 10 m cell does not know how LONG the field is, so 'will it fit' is not answerable here — that belongs to the candidate site finder, which searches for runs of usable ground. What distance legitimately says here is how much MARGINAL ground is usable at all: an aeroplane needing 2,600 ft over a 50 ft obstacle cannot use brush or soft ground the way one needing 900 ft can, because the surface penalty is paid over a longer roll and there is less margin to give away. So it scales the marginal surfaces and stretches the slope curve, and never touches the hazard term — a tower is equally lethal to everything. NOTE ON THE ACTIVE SET: `surface_distance_factor` is reference data about SURFACES and lists open_firm too, but `applies_to` is what the compiler actually scales and deliberately excludes it. Firm open ground is the best ground there is, and keeping it aircraft-independent means the top of the scale does not move underneath a pilot when they switch aeroplanes — what changes is how much of the MARGINAL ground below it they can still use.
